idiom_name: Net::HTTPResponse (each_header + body); mail gem Mail::Message; Struct/Data envelope
implementation_notes: Ruby's packaged messages come from libraries rather than one core type: Net::HTTPResponse exposes each_header for the metadata block and body/read_body for the payload, and the mail gem models the same split as Mail::Message with a Mail::Header of named fields and a Mail::Body holding the (possibly multipart) content. Broker clients follow the same shape - a delivered message object with a properties/headers hash and a payload string - which is the idiomatic Ruby realization: a small class or Struct whose only job is to carry two sections. Nothing in the language fights the pattern, so a hand-written Struct.new(:headers, :body) or Data.define envelope is the fallback when no library fits.
code_sketch:
Message = Struct.new(:headers, :body)

res = Net::HTTP.get_response(uri)
meta = {}
res.each_header { |name, value| meta[name] = value }   # header section
msg = Message.new(meta, res.body)                      # body section

# wire: one package, two sections
wire = [msg.headers.to_json, msg.body].join("\n\n")
pitfalls: Net::HTTP has no single headers hash - each_header/each_capitalized_name iterate, so code expecting a Hash gets an Enumerator and silently reads nothing.
Header injection: values containing CRLF split the header block when interpolated into a hand-built message, so strip/validate newlines before assigning header values.
A shared mutable String payload can be modified in place after it has been handed to a library; dup and freeze the payload when a message must be immutable.
